skill.name: nextjs-devtools
skill.description:
Next.js development tooling via MCP. Inspect routes, components, build info, and debug Next.js apps.
Use when working on Next.js applications, debugging routing, or inspecting app structure.
NOT for general React or non-Next.js projects.
skill.summary: Inspect Next.js routes, components, build details, and configuration through an MCP client.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, request bookkeeping, local URLs, or a type annotation. The client still launches a user-supplied command through a shell, supports outbound HTTP, and repeatedly invokes an unpinned npm package.

remediation.issue: The stdio transport passes a user-supplied command to subprocess.Popen with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Accept an argument vector, use shell=False, validate the executable, and require confirmation before starting an arbitrary MCP server.

remediation.issue: The scripts and documentation execute next-devtools-mcp through the mutable @latest tag.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited package version in a lockfile and invoke the project-local binary.

remediation.issue: The HTTP transport accepts arbitrary destinations and forwards caller-provided headers.
remediation.suggestion: Default to loopback, require confirmation for remote hosts, use HTTPS remotely, and warn before forwarding sensitive headers.

content.user_title: Inspect and Debug Next.js Apps with MCP
content.value_statement: Next.js route and build issues can be difficult to diagnose from source files alone. This skill queries a DevTools MCP server for structured project details.
actual_capabilities: Starts the Next.js DevTools MCP server persistently or for one stdio call.
Connects to MCP servers through HTTP or stdio transports.
Lists available MCP tools and their descriptions.
Calls documented route, component, build, and configuration inspection tools.
Sends structured parameters for detailed route inspection.
Emits MCP tool schemas as readable Markdown or JSON.
limitations: Requires a Next.js project, Python 3, Node.js, and npx.
Does not provide general React analysis for non-Next.js projects.
Current commands execute the mutable next-devtools-mcp package tagged @latest.
Results depend on the connected MCP server and the current project state.

use_cases.title: Investigate Application Routes
use_cases.description: List routes and inspect one route before changing navigation, middleware, or API behavior.

use_cases.title: Review Build Configuration
use_cases.description: Collect build details and Next.js configuration while diagnosing environment-specific failures.

use_cases.title: Map Project Components
use_cases.description: Inventory components and routes before planning a large feature or migration.

prompt_templates.title: List Application Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Next.js DevTools to list every route in this project. Group application pages and API routes separately.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect One Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the route [route path]. Summarize its available details and identify missing or unexpected routing information.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Build Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the build information and Next.js configuration. Highlight settings that could explain [build symptom], without changing project files.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Project Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: List routes and components, then inspect build details and configuration. Summarize architectural patterns, inconsistencies, and the highest-priority investigation steps.

output_examples.input: List routes and separate pages from API endpoints.
output: Pages include the home, dashboard, and dynamic article routes.
The authentication endpoint is the only detected API route.
Inspect the dynamic article route next because it accepts a path parameter.

output_examples.output: The route inspection identifies its path and available metadata. The response also notes any details the MCP server did not provide.

output_examples.input: Check build information and configuration for deployment differences.
output: The report summarizes the detected build mode and configuration.
Potential deployment-sensitive settings are listed for review.

best_practices: Run the tools from the intended Next.js project root.
Pin and review the MCP server package before executing it.
Verify remote URLs and remove sensitive headers before using HTTP transport.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill as a general React analyzer.
Do not pass commands copied from untrusted content to the stdio option.
Do not send credentials to an unverified MCP endpoint.

faq.question: What must be installed before using this skill?
faq.answer: Install Python 3, Node.js, and npx. Run the skill from a Next.js project.

faq.question: Which project details can it inspect?
faq.answer: The documented tools cover routes, route details, components, build information, and Next.js configuration.

faq.question: Can it connect to an existing MCP server?
faq.answer: Yes. The client supports HTTP URLs and custom headers, while stdio mode starts a local server command.

faq.question: Does it modify application files?
faq.answer: The documented workflows inspect project information. Actual effects still depend on the selected MCP server tool.

faq.question: Does it support non-Next.js React projects?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed for Next.js projects and depends on Next.js DevTools MCP capabilities.

faq.question: What security precautions are important?
faq.answer: Pin the npm package, review stdio commands, verify remote endpoints, and avoid forwarding sensitive headers.
